mechanism_688:
One race produces both issues; this section covers the #688 outcome. It predates https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/694: base 547278b9 showed the #688 class in 1 of 12 natural runs.

Sequence, with code at 1e1e1f78:
1. After a clone, handle_new_task single-steps the leader L (task.rs:6008, `self.step_stopped(parent, None)?.next_state().await?`). Its SIGTRAP step stop S (status 0x57f) is collected by the safeptrace notifier worker and queued in the per-tid `pending` FIFO (notifier.rs:869).
2. A non-leader thread's execve reaches de_thread. zap_other_threads SIGKILLs L (signal.c:1348-1351 skips only threads with exit_state set). The fatal signal_wake_up clears JOBCTL_TRACED because L is not PTRACE_FROZEN (sched/signal.h:444-451).
3. So L leaves S with no tracer action and enters its PTRACE_EVENT_EXIT stop (0x6057f). Its message is exactly 0 because group_exec_task is set (exit.c:1100-1101). Kernel investigation S6: 8 of 8 per mode. Measured message: 0 in more than 1760 reads.
4. The worker publishes that EXIT stop out of band with publish_exit_stop (notifier.rs:766). This sets exit_status to EXIT_STOPPED and the capability to AVAILABLE.
5. The run loop has already decoded S. handle_sigtrap's default branch (task.rs:3638) calls resume_stopped (5444), which issues PTRACE_CONT. The kernel binds a resume to whatever stop the tracee is in now (ptrace.c:193-195), so this stale CONT consumes the EXIT stop.
   - Forced-run backtrace: resume_stopped <- handle_sigtrap:3638 <- handle_signal:3858 <- handle_stop_event:3154 <- run_loop_events:6341 <- run_loop:6225 <- ordinary_start:6642.
   - Natural timing: the notifier had latched 0x6057f 3.2 to 136.6 microseconds before the CONT in 6 of 7 instances. In run-47 the gap was -0.7 microseconds, which is within probe resolution.
6. finish_ordinary_terminal (tracer.rs about 505-722) then calls PTRACE_GETEVENTMSG and gets ESRCH, because L is no longer in a stop. de_thread then releases the old leader.
   - waitid and /proc cannot supply the status afterwards: ECHILD at exec, then release_task.
7. The Exec edge carries exit_status None. The code holds HeldRootStop and calls session.retry_after(ExitEventStatusUnavailable{pid, former}) (tracer.rs:666-699). retry_after is refuse_cleanup (task.rs:1308/1461): session.fail, a recorded cleanup_refusal, CleanupPending, then wait_retry(epoch). It does not busy-spin, but it never completes, so the test hits the 3 s Pending panic.

Correction to the kernel investigator: the Err(Died) comment blames 'a timer step'. The empirical investigator refuted that for all 17 instances, and all agree the resume came from reverie. In natural runs the caller is inferred from site 5444 plus the preceding stop kind; a backtrace exists only for the forced run.

Why '0 on ESRCH' would be unsound: a leader that self-exits (SYS_exit(N), thread-only) holds a real message N<<8. The zap then wakes it out of that EXIT stop and reads return ESRCH (kernel S3a, 250 of 250). 'Exec edge + ESRCH => Exited(0)' would therefore fabricate a status.

Why check-then-resume only narrows the window: ptrace freezes the tracee per request (ptrace.c:184-219), so there is no compare-and-resume. Any WNOHANG or GETSIGINFO check before PTRACE_CONT leaves a time-of-check to time-of-use gap. The kernel investigator's fix suggestion 3 is therefore a narrowing, not a fix, and the empirical investigator is right.

Latent outcome D, never observed: the stale CONT lands after the kernel conversion but before the worker's waitid collects the EXIT. After a resume takes effect, an unreported EXIT stop is no longer reportable (S6), so that EXIT is never collected. The leader's run loop would then receive Exec(former != tid), which handle_exec_event (task.rs:3908) treats as the leader's own exec.

Rates:
- Empirical, load about 130: 5 of 62 runs failed, 7 of 371 exec edges (1.9%).
- Sigtrap investigator, taskset to 2 CPUs: 0 of 20.
- The rate is strongly load-dependent.
mechanism_686:
This is the same conversion as #688 with a different interleaving. S is still queued in the FIFO when the kernel turns it into L's EXIT stop.

Sequence:
1. drive_ordinary (task.rs:6928-6937) uses select_biased! in the order cancelled, global_failure, exit, run_loop. The exit future (the out-of-band EXIT publication) wins, and the run loop is dropped before it pops S.
2. finish_ordinary_terminal reads getevent. This succeeds and returns 0.
3. It resumes the EXIT capability (resume_retaining, tracer.rs:592). Its next owned wait pops the FIFO front (notifier.rs:661/3208). That front is the stale S (0x57f), not the Exec (0x4057f), which is queued behind S.
4. The `else if event != Event::Exit` arm (tracer.rs:710-716) calls session.fail("unexpected ptrace terminal stop") and signal_groups. The real Exec is never consumed.
5. The code then sets `current = Ok(stopped)` (717). Where that path continues, getevent could be called again on a non-EXIT stop, a latent re-entry.

Why S is stale: the tracee left it without any tracer request, through the fatal wake that produced this very EXIT (sched/signal.h:444-451). It can never be resumed, and no later event can be queued ahead of the EXIT. So the FIFO entries queued before the EXIT publication are provably dead. Entries queued after it, such as the Exec, are live.

The same stale front also hurts the legacy/LiteInst `run` path (task.rs:7109). It races exit_event, then wait_after_exit_event, then assume_exited(), which panics on a stale Stopped.

Outcome C (empirical run-48, passing) is inferred as: S was decoded, then the run loop was dropped before the CONT was issued. The decider is whether run-48's probe log shows a decode of 0x57f.

Harness half of #686: ordinary_exec_owner_control (tracer.rs:5851) accepts any Ok(ToolRunOutcome::Complete(completed)) at about 5960. It runs the elapsed, root-absent and timer assertions (for example `timers.len()==1` at about 6006) before it inspects completed.result. So a Complete(Err) reports a misleading timer or elapsed assertion instead of the error. The final result checks do catch Err (fail=false unwraps; fail=true requires NonleaderFailure), so measured false passes are 0 of 140. The defect is misattribution, and the fix must strengthen the checks by moving and extending them, not relaxing them.

Rates:
- Base: SIGTRAP 3 of 12 natural and 4 of 4 forced.
- #686 issue table: 52 of 300 at base and 58 of 300 at the fix; 44 and 37 of 200 pinned.
- Sigtrap investigator at the head, 2 CPUs: 3 of 20.
- Forced with SIGTRAP_FORCE_DELAY_MS=200: 9 of 9 at both head and base.

options.name: A. safeptrace supersession fence plus the existing honest refusal for the residual
options.files: safeptrace/src/lib.rs (Stopped::resume ~776, resume_retaining ~790, step ~826, syscall ~833, detach ~970, map_err, Error enum); safeptrace/src/notifier.rs (Event exit_status read helper beside exit_stop_observed ~3158); reverie-ptrace/src/task.rs (drive_ordinary ~6905-6990, legacy run ~7109, resume_stopped/step_stopped/syscall_stopped 5435-5468 error mapping); reverie-ptrace/src/tracer.rs (RootStopLease resume/step/syscall/detach ~940-990, raw legacy CONTs at 1903/1923 audited)
options.change:
1. Resume-family requests on a non-EXIT Stopped (resume, step, syscall, detach) check the tid's Event.exit_status first. If it is EXIT_STOPPED, the request is refused without calling ptrace.
   - The refusal is a new typed variant, for example Error::Superseded{pid}. It must NOT reuse Died, because Zombie::reap panics on non-Exit stops.
   - The refusal carries no capability.
   - A Stopped minted from the claimed EXIT capability must be distinguishable and exempt, because resume_retaining on the EXIT stop is what de_thread waits for.
2. drive_ordinary maps a run-loop Err(Superseded) to a single await of the already-raced exit_event, the same as Left.
3. The legacy run gets the equivalent mapping.
4. Every raw-CONT site is audited: notifier.rs 1941, 3845, 3892, 4228; tracer.rs 1903, 1923. The cleanup sites already run revoke_unclaimed_exit_stop, and that behaviour is kept.
5. The exit owner then reads the real kernel message (0) through getevent.
6. The residual keeps the existing typed ExitEventStatusUnavailable path unchanged. The residual is the case where the kernel converted S but the worker had not yet published at check time, plus latent D.
options.tool_visible_effect:
The Tool sees:
- Normal exec (no conversion race): unchanged, on_exit_thread(old leader, Exited(0)) from the real getevent.
- EXIT published before the stale resume (6 of 7 natural instances): base gave CleanupPending/ExitEventStatusUnavailable, with no on_exit_thread for the old leader and the run Pending. A gives on_exit_thread(old leader, Exited(0)) read from the kernel and a Complete run.
- Conversion not yet published at check time (residual; run-47 -0.7 microseconds is the candidate): the same as base, a typed CleanupPending with an ExitEventStatusUnavailable primary. It is honest, but the Tool view stays nondeterministic across runs at a lower rate.
- Latent D (EXIT never collected): unchanged from base (unobserved).
- Self-exit leader (S3a): unchanged. The real N<<8 is delivered when getevent succeeds; otherwise the typed refusal.
- Group kill (no Exec): unchanged. The Died path reaps a real terminal status.
options.constraint_check:
- Retry: none added. Superseded leads to one await of an existing future. retry_after is not extended.
- Deadline: the 3 s predicate is unchanged; no timeout is touched.
- Fabricated status: none. The status reaching retire_replaced_leader -> on_exit_thread is only ever the kernel's getevent value; undeterminable cases keep the typed refusal.
- Comparator or assertion change: none. fatal_exit_payload_tests::actual_exec_without_prior_payload_retains_same_owner_across_refusal stays byte-identical. New tests only add checks.
- Determinism: A strictly reduces the rate of the nondeterministic outcome but does not eliminate it.
options.kernel_basis:
- Conversion: signal.c:1348-1351 and sched/signal.h:444-451.
- Resume binds to the current stop: ptrace.c:193-195.
- Zap message is 0: exit.c:1100-1101.
- Exec proves no group kill won: fs/exec.c:913-920.
- The fence works because, once the worker has latched EXIT for this tid, any stop the tracer believes it holds for that tid is dead. A tracee reports its EXIT only after leaving every earlier stop, and a tid never stops again after EXIT except by resuming it.
options.risks:
- Time-of-check to time-of-use residual: the fence narrows the window and does not close it.
- Every resume-family entry point must be covered: 25 resume_stopped, 16 step_stopped, 2 syscall_stopped, 12 .resume(, 5 .step(, 6 .syscall( and 1 resume_retaining call sites in reverie-ptrace/src.
- Callers that `?` the new error must route it to the exit owner, not to session failure.
- Adding a public Error variant to safeptrace is an API change for matchers: exhaustive matches break at compile time, which is a feature.
- Distinguishing the EXIT-capability Stopped needs a flag carried from the claim.
options.tests_and_mutations:
Deterministic forced-window test T1, a test-only seam like EXIT_RESUME_CONTROL:
- Park the leader's post-clone resume at handle_sigtrap:3638 until notifier exit_status == EXIT_STOPPED for that tid. Poll a condition, no sleep; the empirical PROBE_DELAY_LEADER_CONT_US=3000 reproduced 5/6, 5/5 and 1/1.
- Base (1e1e) fails with ExitEventStatusUnavailable. A passes with Complete, on_exit_thread(old, Exited(0)) and stdout 'survived'.

Residual test T2:
- Park after the fence check and before the ptrace syscall until the worker publishes EXIT.
- Must yield exactly the typed CleanupPending with an ExitEventStatusUnavailable primary, no consuming hooks, and the held stop retained. This is the existing contract.

Unit tests in safeptrace:
- Superseded is returned for resume, step, syscall and detach on a non-EXIT Stopped when EXIT_STOPPED is set.
- The EXIT-capability resume_retaining is not refused.

Mutations, each must fail a test:
- (m1) Delete the fence check: T1 fails.
- (m2) Exempt all Stopped from the fence: T1 fails.
- (m3) Map Superseded to session.fail instead of the exit await: T1 fails with a failure primary.
- (m4) Reuse Died for the refusal: the Zombie::reap panic, caught by T1.
- (m5) Remove the exemption for the EXIT capability: every exec test hangs past 3 s.

Campaigns at the fix head compared with 1e1e: 40x ordinary_nonleader and 40x ordinary_nonleader_exec.

options.name: B. A plus a proven derivation of the zap status from a resume-intent generation
options.files: As A, plus safeptrace/src/notifier.rs (Event: AtomicU64 resume_gen; worker snapshot at each status collection; publish_exit_stop records the snapshot and the previous stop's snapshot); every resume site in safeptrace lib.rs 777/794/827/834/971 and notifier.rs 1941/3845/3892/4228; reverie-ptrace/src/tracer.rs 1903/1923 and finish_ordinary_terminal Exec edge (666-699)
options.change:
1. Each Event gets a generation counter G.
   - Every resume-family ptrace request on the tid (including PTRACE_KILL, detach and the raw notifier/cleanup CONTs) does G.fetch_add(SeqCst) BEFORE the fence check and the syscall.
   - The worker loads G immediately after each waitid return, storing g_prev for the last non-EXIT stop and g_exit for the EXIT.
2. At the Exec edge with getevent == ESRCH:
   - If an EXIT for this tid was collected and g_exit == g_prev, derive Exited(0).
   - Otherwise take the existing typed ExitEventStatusUnavailable path.
3. Why the derivation is sound, when every resume bumps G:
   - g_exit == g_prev proves no resume was issued between collecting the held stop and collecting the EXIT.
   - So L left its held stop only through a fatal wake.
   - The Exec proves that wake was the exec zap (fs/exec.c:913-920), and the zap message is 0 (exit.c:1100-1101).
4. The self-exit case always shows g_exit != g_prev, because L must have been resumed to call SYS_exit, so it is refused.
5. The Exec-edge comment ('Losing the old EXIT payload cannot authorize a fabricated consuming hook') must be rewritten to document the proof.
options.tool_visible_effect:
Same as A, plus:
- EXIT collected before the tracer's fetch_add for the stale resume, including the 'published after the fence check' part of A's residual: base gave CleanupPending. B gives on_exit_thread(old, Exited(0)), a value the kernel defines for this case (proved from observation, not read from getevent).
- Remaining residual (fetch_add then conversion then collection, or latent D): typed CleanupPending as base.
- Self-exit (S3a): never Exited(0). The real N<<8 when read, otherwise the typed refusal.
options.constraint_check:
- Retry: none.
- Deadline: none widened.
- Fabricated status: arguable. Exited(0) is derived, not read, but from a proof over observed facts: an Exec, a collected EXIT, and an unchanged generation. It must be reviewed as such. If the reviewer rejects derivation-by-proof as 'fabrication', B is out.
- Comparator or assertion change: none. The existing erase-payload test erases the payload without the generation proof, so it still gets the refusal. Verify that the seam erases in a way that leaves g_exit != g_prev, or keep it on the refusal branch explicitly.
- Determinism: better than A, still not complete.
options.kernel_basis:
As A, plus:
- The kernel only leaves a ptrace stop without a tracer request through a fatal wake.
- In a thread group that later reports PTRACE_EVENT_EXEC, the only fatal wake is de_thread's zap.
- Zap-killed exit code 0: exit.c:1100-1101.
options.risks:
- One missed resume site (including a future one) makes the derivation unsound, a silent wrong status.
- The residual is dominated by preemption between fetch_add and the syscall, so the gain over A is small.
- Contradicts the current contract comment.
- More review surface in a crate shared by all backends.
options.tests_and_mutations:
- T1 and T2 as in A.
- T3: park the worker between waitid return and its G load while the tracer issues the stale resume. Must refuse (g_exit != g_prev).
- T4: park the tracer after fetch_add and before the syscall until EXIT is collected. Must refuse.
- T5: force collection of EXIT before the tracer's fetch_add, then let the CONT consume it. Must deliver Exited(0) through derivation.
- Self-exit fixture (real_exit_resume_control-style SYS_exit(23), payload 23<<8) with a forced zap after the EXIT: must NEVER report Exited(0).

Mutations, each must fail a test:
- (m6) Remove the G bump at one site, such as notifier.rs 3845 or detach: T3/T4 or the self-exit fixture fails.
- (m7) Derive 0 when g_exit != g_prev: the self-exit fixture fails.
- (m8) Load G before waitid instead of after: T4 fails.

options.name: C. Exec-in-flight group resume barrier, which makes the conversion race unreachable
options.files: reverie-ptrace/src/tracer.rs seccomp_filter (~3895): unconditional Action::Trace for execve and execveat, handled internally when the Tool is not subscribed; reverie-ptrace/src/task.rs (the execve seccomp-stop path and injection that already returns Event::Exec / Event::Syscall ~7870-7910; process_state gains an exec_in_flight count; resume_stopped/step_stopped/syscall_stopped and RootStopLease consult it; handle_exec_event / drive_ordinary resolve it); reverie-ptrace/src/seccomp_ip_window_tests.rs expectations for the 'none' filter
options.change:
1. The tracer always traps execve and execveat.
   - Before resuming the exec'ing thread from its execve seccomp stop, it sets a per-thread-group exec_in_flight marker.
   - It resumes that thread with syscall-stepping (the existing injection path), so failure is observed as Event::Syscall with -errno.
2. While the marker is set, any resume-family request for another thread of the group is withheld as an await on the marker's resolution, not a poll. The EXIT-capability resume stays exempt, because de_thread waits on it.
3. Resolution:
   - On Exec: withheld requests resolve to Superseded and go to the exit future. The kernel has turned each held stop into an EXIT stop, which the exit owner reads with getevent (0).
   - On execve failure: withheld requests are issued normally, because nothing was zapped before the point of no return.
4. Why this is race-free: all ptrace requests for a thread group come from the single attaching OS thread; a request from any other thread gets ESRCH (ptrace.c:251). So the marker write and every sibling resume are totally ordered with no lock.
   - Any sibling resume issued before the exec'er is resumed hits a live stop, because the zap cannot happen before the exec'er runs.
   - Any sibling resume issued after it is withheld.
5. Recommended with a debug assertion: if a resume ever sees EXIT_STOPPED during a barrier, fail fast with a typed error.
options.tool_visible_effect:
The Tool sees:
- Normal exec: on_exit_thread(old, Exited(0)) from getevent, as base.
- Every conversion-race interleaving from a trapped execve (#688 outcome A, latent D, the #686 feed): the old leader's EXIT stop is always held for the exit owner, so the Tool always sees on_exit_thread(old, Exited(0)) read from the kernel and the run Completes. This is deterministic, where base was sometimes CleanupPending or a session failure.
- Siblings during execve: stops reached after the barrier are held until resolution. With a successful exec they see only on_exit_thread. A sibling syscall that reached its seccomp stop but never executed is not reported; base reported it only when it won a race. If the barrier is placed before Tool dispatch, this removes a timing-dependent Tool event. If placed at the resume, a Tool handler's injection returns the existing thread-exited error. Pick dispatch-boundary placement for determinism.
- Failed execve: siblings stall only for the pre-point-of-no-return duration, then proceed as base.
- Tools not subscribed to execve: they now incur an internal seccomp stop per execve. The Tool sees no event, but Stats::seccomp_stops counts it.
- Undeterminable case: unreachable for trapped execs. The existing typed ExitEventStatusUnavailable stays as the fail-safe for anything that escapes, such as a compat-ABI execve if not trapped.
options.constraint_check:
- Retry: none. The withheld request is one await on a resolution event, with no loop.
- Deadline: none added or widened. The barrier has no timeout, which is the liveness risk below.
- Fabricated status: none. The old leader's status is always the kernel's getevent value.
- Comparator or assertion change: the seccomp_ip_window_tests expectation for Subscription::none() must now include execve/execveat traces. That is a changed expected value and must be reviewed as a deliberate contract change, not weakening. It is stricter: more is traced. The existing retained-refusal test is unchanged.
- Determinism: closes the race for ordinary mode.
options.kernel_basis:
- The zap happens only after the exec'er passes the point of no return in begin_new_exec/de_thread.
- de_thread waits for the old leader's exit_state, which requires the tracer to resume its EXIT stop.
- Held stops are converted by the fatal wake: sched/signal.h:444-451.
- Single-tracer-thread rule: ptrace.c:251.
- Zap message is 0: exit.c:1100-1101.
options.risks:
- Liveness: execve pre-point-of-no-return work could depend on a sibling (userfaultfd-backed filename or argv pages served by a sibling, a FUSE server thread in the same group). That is a deadlock with no deadline.
- Semantic change: siblings stall during execve. POSIX allows arbitrary delay.
- Largest change: seccomp filter plus group state plus every resume entry point.
- Needs a deterministic-scheduling-review, because this is a scheduling and ordering change.
- Compat execve (int 0x80, nr 11) coverage must be checked.
- Extra seccomp stop cost per exec.
options.tests_and_mutations:
- T1 and the #686 forced test T6 (below) must pass with no refusal.
- T7: park the exec'er at its execve seccomp stop, force a sibling step stop to be collected, release the exec'er. The sibling's resume must be withheld and then superseded, and the old leader must deliver Exited(0).
- T8: failing execve (ENOENT) with a sibling held. The sibling must resume and the run must Complete with the sibling's output.
- T9: a Tool with no execve subscription must still get the barrier, and must see no handle_syscall_event for execve.
- 40+40 campaigns.

Mutations, each must fail a test:
- (m9) Set the marker after resuming the exec'er instead of before: T7 fails.
- (m10) Drop the unconditional execve trace: T9 and T1 fail.
- (m11) Never release on failure: T8 hangs and the 3 s predicate fails.
- (m12) Withhold the EXIT-capability resume too: every exec test fails.

options.name: D. Surface the undeterminable case as fail-fast or a Tool-expressible 'status unavailable' (owner contract decision; combinable with A/B/C)
options.files: reverie-process/src/exit_status.rs (ExitStatus); reverie/src/tool.rs:679 (on_exit_thread); reverie-ptrace/src/task.rs retire_replaced_leader (~6849) and OrdinaryTerminal::Exec (~6737-6845); tracer.rs finish_ordinary_terminal Exec edge (666-699); fatal_exit_payload_tests.rs
options.change:
Two variants.

D1, fail-fast:
- Replace the retained retry_after Pending with session.fail(ExitEventStatusUnavailable) plus teardown, so the run ends promptly with a typed error rather than Pending at the 3 s predicate.
- The replaced leader's thread_state is dropped with no on_exit_thread call, because there is no status to pass.

D2, new contract:
- Add an explicit 'unavailable' outcome, for example a new on_exit_thread_status_unavailable hook or an ExitStatus-adjacent enum, so the Tool is told honestly.
options.tool_visible_effect:
Applies only in the undeterminable case (A/B residual, latent D). Every other case is unchanged.
- D1: base left the Tool waiting on CleanupPending until external teardown. D1 ends the run with Err(ExitEventStatusUnavailable) immediately. The old leader's on_exit_thread is never called in either.
- D2: the Tool receives an explicit status-unavailable callback for the old leader. This is a public API change for all Tools.
options.constraint_check:
- Retry: D removes a wait; it adds none.
- Deadline: none.
- Fabricated status: none.
- Comparator or assertion change: D1 changes the expected outcome of actual_exec_without_prior_payload_retains_same_owner_across_refusal (from retained CleanupPending across 2 attempts to fail-fast). That is a contract change that reviewers must approve explicitly; done silently it would read as weakening. D2 is additive.
- Determinism: does not reduce the rate. It only changes how the residual is reported.
options.kernel_basis:
The residual is genuinely undeterminable:
- The payload was consumed.
- waitid gets ECHILD and /proc is gone after release_task.
- S3a proves a self-exit leader can reach the same ESRCH with a nonzero status.
options.risks:
- Owner decision required.
- D2 touches the reverie public Tool trait, which Hermit implements.
- D1 alters existing test expectations.
- D alone does not fix #688's rate.
options.tests_and_mutations:
- D1: the forced residual seam (T2) must yield a prompt Err with an ExitEventStatusUnavailable primary well inside 3 s, and no consuming hooks.
  - Mutation: revert to retry_after, and the prompt-Err assertion fails.
- D2: T2 must invoke the unavailable hook exactly once and on_exit_thread zero times.
  - Mutation: call on_exit_thread(Exited(0)) instead, and the test fails.

options.name: #686 handling (applies with any option): retire the provably dead pre-EXIT FIFO entries, fix the non-EXIT re-entry, strengthen the harness
options.files: safeptrace/src/notifier.rs (StatusState: pre_exit_len; publish_exit_stop ~766 under exit_publication then status lock, same order as publish_terminal_exit_state ~802; the EXIT-capability resume path used by Stopped::resume/resume_retaining in lib.rs ~776/790; update_sync_status ~887 for the sync path); reverie-ptrace/src/tracer.rs finish_ordinary_terminal (710-717) and ordinary_exec_owner_control (~5851, extraction ~5960)
options.change:
1. In publish_exit_stop, record pre_exit_len = pending.len() atomically with the publication.
2. When the claimed EXIT capability is resumed, pop exactly pre_exit_len entries from the FIFO front, and record them in a diagnostics counter.
   - These are stops the tracee left with no request, through the fatal wake that produced this EXIT.
   - Entries queued after the publication (the Exec 0x4057f) are never touched.
   - Apply the same rule on the sync path, where the EXIT goes through the FIFO: retire the entries ahead of it when the EXIT is consumed.
3. In finish_ordinary_terminal, replace `current = Ok(stopped)` after the non-EXIT arm with a terminal return, so getevent is never called on a non-EXIT stop. The session.fail message and label are unchanged; that arm becomes reachable only by a genuinely unexpected stop.
4. Harness, in ordinary_exec_owner_control immediately after `completed` is extracted (~5960) and before the elapsed, root-absent and timer assertions:
   - fail=false: `completed.result.as_ref().unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("exec owner completed with error: {e:?}"))`, then assert Exited(0), stdout 'survived', stderr ''.
   - fail=true: `expect_err("displaced leader Tool failure lost")`, NonleaderFailure primary, phase 'ptrace replaced leader on_exit_thread', former Signaled(SIGKILL).
   - Keep every later check unchanged.
options.tool_visible_effect:
The Tool sees:
- Stale S queued before EXIT (#686): base gave session failure 'unexpected ptrace terminal stop', the Exec lost, and no on_exit_thread for the old leader. Now the Exec is consumed and the Tool sees on_exit_thread(old, Exited(0)) from the real getevent, then the new leader's run. The run Completes.
- No stale entry: unchanged.
- A genuinely unexpected non-EXIT stop after the EXIT resume: session failure as base, with no latent getevent re-entry.
- Legacy/LiteInst run: no assume_exited panic on a stale Stopped.
- Harness: only which assertion reports a Complete(Err) changes. It now reports the error itself rather than a timer or elapsed symptom. Measured false passes: 0 of 140.
options.constraint_check:
- Retry: none.
- Deadline: none.
- Fabricated status: none; only kernel-defined dead stops are discarded, and statuses come from getevent.
- Comparator or assertion change: the harness checks are strictly added or moved earlier. The later identical checks remain, and no label or message is altered.
- Determinism: removes a nondeterministic session failure.
options.kernel_basis:
- A fatal wake clears TRACED for a non-frozen tracee (sched/signal.h:444-451). A stop it leaves this way can never be resumed.
- Every status the kernel reports before PTRACE_EVENT_EXIT belongs to a stop the tracee has already left, so it cannot be resumed afterwards. Statuses reported after it (Exec on the new leader's tid under the same pid) are live.
- The lock order exit_publication then status matches publish_terminal_exit_state.
options.risks:
- Getting pre_exit_len wrong in either direction loses the Exec (drain too many) or keeps #686 (drain too few).
- The sync path (update_sync_status) queues EXIT inside the FIFO and needs its own boundary.
- A reservation (reserve_pending_for_cleanup) held across retirement must be handled: retirement must take the same status lock.
options.tests_and_mutations:
Deterministic T6, a test-only seam:
- Hold the run loop between step_stopped and next_state at task.rs:6008 until the leader's EXIT is published, so S stays queued. SIGTRAP_FORCE_DELAY_MS=200 failed 9/9 at both head and base.
- 1e1e fails with 'unexpected ptrace terminal stop'. The fix passes with Complete and on_exit_thread(old, Exited(0)).

Unit test in notifier:
- Push S, publish EXIT, push Exec, resume the EXIT capability.
- The FIFO front must be Exec, and the retired count must be 1.

Harness self-check:
- A unit case feeding a synthetic Complete(Err) into the extracted-result check must panic with 'exec owner completed with error'.

Mutations, each must fail a test:
- (m13) Skip retirement: T6 fails.
- (m14) Drain the whole FIFO: the unit test fails (Exec lost) and T6 hangs.
- (m15) Record pre_exit_len outside the lock: a stress unit test with a racing push fails.
- (m16) Restore `current = Ok(stopped)`: a seam test forcing a non-EXIT stop after the resume must show exactly one session failure and no getevent on the non-EXIT stop.
- (m17) Move the harness result check back after the timer assertion: the synthetic Complete(Err) case reports the timer message and fails.

recommended:
Recommended: the #686 handling plus option A now, with option C as the follow-up that closes the residual. Option D goes to the owner as a decision. Option B is not recommended.

Why A first:
- It is small and local to safeptrace plus the drive_ordinary mapping.
- It never fabricates a status.
- It keeps every existing test byte-identical, including the retained-refusal contract.
- It removes the dominant natural #688 interleaving: EXIT latched 3.2 to 136.6 microseconds before the stale CONT in 6 of 7 measured instances.
- The #686 FIFO retirement removes the SIGTRAP outcome entirely. The dead entries are defined exactly by the kernel.

What A leaves open:
- A does not make the Tool view deterministic. A residual stays when the conversion has not yet been published at check time (run-47 at -0.7 microseconds is the candidate), plus latent D.
- My arithmetic, not measured: residual is about 1 in 7 of 7/371 exec edges, and about 6 edges per run. That gives roughly a 1-2% chance of failure per run under load, so 0/40 is not guaranteed on A alone.

Why C next:
- C is the only option that makes the conversion race unreachable. A single tracer thread orders all requests for a thread group, and an exec-in-flight barrier set before the exec'er resumes closes the window without a lock.
- It carries a liveness risk (execve depending on a sibling) and a seccomp-filter contract change. It should go through a deterministic-scheduling-review rather than being bundled into the #688 hotfix.
- If the owner prefers one change that meets 0/40 by construction, take C together with the #686 handling, and treat A's fence as the fail-fast guard inside C.

Why not B: its gain over A is small (the residual is dominated by preemption between the counter bump and the syscall). One missed site makes it silently unsound, and whether 'derived by proof' counts as 'fabricated' is contestable under the hard constraint.

The size of A's residual is unknown. Run-47 at -0.7 microseconds is within probe resolution, so it is not certain that the EXIT was unpublished at check time. The decider is a higher-resolution probe of the publication versus the fence check.

Latent outcome D is unobserved: the stale CONT lands before the worker collects the EXIT, and the leader's run loop then receives Exec(former != tid), which handle_exec_event (task.rs:3908) would treat as the leader's own exec. There is no test seam yet. A forced test is needed to show what base and A do.
The natural-run caller of the stale resume is inferred from ptrace site 5444 and the preceding stop kind. A backtrace exists only for the forced run. The decider is a caller tag in natural runs.
Run-48 (outcome C, passing) interpretation: whether its probe log shows a decode of 0x57f before the run loop was dropped.
The Tool contract has no 'status unavailable' outcome. ExitStatus is only Exited or Signaled, and on_exit_thread at reverie/src/tool.rs:679 requires one. Option D needs an owner decision.

Option C liveness: execve work before the point of no return that depends on a sibling (userfaultfd, or a FUSE server thread in the same group) would deadlock with no deadline. Coverage of compat-ABI execve (int 0x80) by the seccomp filter is unchecked.
Other nested-step sites share the conversion exposure: task.rs 2719, 3980, 4144, 7336, 7644 and timer.rs 1518. A and C cover them generically. Narrowing only the post-clone step at 6008 would not.

The complete resume-site enumeration must be verified by review: safeptrace lib.rs 777/794/827/834/971, notifier.rs 1941/3845/3892/4228, tracer.rs 1903/1923, and stack.rs 316 (test). A needs full coverage for effectiveness; B needs it for soundness.

Assumption that all ptrace requests for a thread group come from one OS thread: requests from any other thread get ESRCH (ptrace.c:251). Options C and A rely on this, and it is not verified against reverie's runtime threading.
Kernel source is upstream v7.1 read against a vendor 7.1.3 build. The kernel investigation's campaign 2 (N=200) never ran, and S6 has only 8 runs per mode.
The S5 partial lead for #686 (a SINGLESTEP at the exec event produces a post-exec SIGTRAP) rests on 5 runs. It is unrelated to the FIFO mechanism, but it could be a second SIGTRAP producer.
The sync-path boundary for the #686 retirement (update_sync_status queues EXIT inside the FIFO) and its interaction with reserve_pending_for_cleanup reservations need a design check in code review.
The cross-load rate differences (1.9% of exec edges at load about 130, against 0/20 on 2 pinned CPUs) mean the 40-run campaigns must record load, or a 0/40 may just be a quiet host.
